name: Aleksandar Radovanović
funLine: I enjoy cooking, cycling, and skiing. But my favourite way to spend time away from work is playing with my child.
bio: I have around five years of experience in software development, and I currently work as a Development Lead on the Compass project. My role combines leading the development team, helping manage the project from the technical side, and working with clients to define requirements. What I enjoy most is building software that makes a real difference: helping people work more efficiently, simplifying everyday tasks, and making business processes easier through digitalisation.

I enjoy working with both clients and the team. With clients, I like to ask questions, explore the details, and understand what they really need rather than simply take a request at face value. Once we understand the problem, my job is to help the team turn that understanding into a solution that works in practice. I want everyone to have the information, support, and motivation they need to do their best work.

When I face a difficult problem, I start by breaking it down into smaller, manageable pieces. We work through them one by one and then bring everything together into a solution. I also like to look at a problem from different angles and hear different opinions. I believe the best solutions often come from combining several perspectives, and I want everyone on the team to feel comfortable contributing their ideas.

I studied Electronics and Computer Engineering at the Higher School of Technical Vocational Studies in Čačak. Software development was not originally my main goal; I was more interested in electronics. What attracted me was the possibility of bringing electronics and software engineering together. Over time, software development became a field in which I could combine technical thinking, creativity, and practical problem-solving.

One thing that defines my approach is that I give every problem a thorough look, regardless of its size. I like to analyse the details, research the context, and understand the bigger picture before deciding how to move forward. Having worked across different types of businesses and organisational environments has also taught me that a solution that looks good on paper does not always work in reality. I try to understand how things actually operate, because that is where good engineering decisions begin.
outsideWork: Outside work, I enjoy cooking, especially trying things out in the kitchen and preparing something good from scratch. I also train regularly, ride my bike, and go skiing whenever I get the chance. But the best part of my free time is spending it with my child, playing together and enjoying the little things. It is a good reminder that the most valuable moments are often the simplest ones.
